Identification of Waterlogging Locations Using LiDAR-Derived Terrain Analysis

A campus-scale terrain analysis workflow to identify low-lying depressions and screen potential waterlogging locations. The mapped locations are preliminary candidates and require field verification.

Study area: 500 m × 500 mCoordinate system: WGS 84 / UTM Zone 43N (EPSG:32643)Data: IIT Roorkee campus LiDAR

Processing workflow

Summary of the analysis sequence used to produce the screening outputs

01

LiDAR preparation

Campus point cloud clipped to the 500 m × 500 m study area; statistical outlier filtering applied (K=8, multiplier=2).

02

Ground classification

SMRF classification produced 14,961,933 ground points from the filtered point cloud.

03

DTM generation

Ground points interpolated using a linear TIN to a 0.5 m raster DTM (1000 × 1000 cells).

04

Depression screening

Wang and Liu Fill Sinks and terrain thresholds used to map depressions and shortlist candidate locations.

Interpretation and limitations

Important context for responsible use of the dashboard

Preliminary screening only. The 12 mapped polygons represent potential low-lying waterlogging locations inferred from LiDAR-derived terrain. They are not confirmed waterlogging observations. Site inspection, drainage-condition checks, and/or post-rainfall validation are needed before operational use.
Accuracy assessment not yet available. No field/drone validation or formal Precision, Recall, F1-score, or IoU metrics were reported. The vertical datum of the source LiDAR is undocumented; building footprints may be approximate due to interpolation; SMRF parameters were not tuned against independent reference data.
Candidate-count reconciliation: Run-5 CSV reports 65 candidate spots; the intermediate processing outputs include 134 raw polygons and 132 depth-statistics polygons; the final frozen GeoPackage contains 12 candidate polygons. These are different processing stages and must not be treated as equivalent counts. The final 12 polygons have a combined geometric area of 17.75 m² (stored attributes total 17.73 m²).
Project: CEC201 · Team 2 · IIT Roorkee
Software reported: QGIS 4.0.0, PDAL 2.9.3, GDAL 3.12.0. Depression filling: Wang and Liu algorithm.
Dashboard content is based on the team's project report and its embedded figures. Values are presented as reported; this dashboard does not independently validate the analysis.
